subtitles.text: overspending, and lower than normal attendance.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Several costly acquisitions in recent years sunk the museum into spiraling debt.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: When repairs to the facilities became unavoidable and visitor attendance fell,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: it became clear that a major influx of cash was needed to cure the museum's ills.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: In June, the decision was made to auction off several of its older exhibits.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: That decision paid off well yesterday.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The four items that the unidentified bidder purchased included:

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: the Toltec Mayan ceremonial coffer,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: King Richard the Lionheart's sword from the Crusades,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Leonardo da Vinci's Codex Atlanticus,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: and an interactive sculpture entitled Self-Awareness, credited to Kenneth Farnstein.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Attendees of the auction said the buyer did not try to purchase any other items,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: but immediately made an excessive bid on these four artifacts as soon as the bidding opened.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Experts estimated that the unidentified man paid at least seven billion credits more than the true value of the pieces,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: but none could say why he was so interested in four such disparate artifacts.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: They eventually conceded that it may have simply been their rich histories that intrigued him.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The opinion originally held by the majority of races represented at the talks

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: is that time travel technology is an invaluable tool for self-discovery

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: and, as such, should not be denied to any race.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: However, the Laxonie abandoned this position last week in favor of destroying the technology.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Presumably, this sudden change of opinion was due in large part to the arrest of Agent 5,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: an unfortunate illustration of the danger of time travel.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The Dorlün and Zâng-traqar on the other hand, have continued to cling tightly to their convictions.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: They're of the opinion that this technology is far too important to be buried because of paranoia.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Time travel, the Zangtrakar argue, is like any other powerful tool.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: It represents a danger only if the user doesn't have the insight to take the proper precautions.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: And, if care is taken, there should be no reason whatsoever

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: to fear what should be the greatest advance the Symbiotry has ever known.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Perhaps Grandon Farlink, the Dorlün emissary, stated the feelings of these two races most eloquently:

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: "At long last," he said. "We can all be in touch with our pasts."

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: "Each race can now know the truths of its history,"

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: "no longer must time be wasted with painstaking research and endless conjecture,"

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: "only to arrive at an uncertain understanding of the events that shaped history."

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: "The answers, all of the answers, lie within our reach if only we have the will to grasp for them."

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The third viewpoint, which was originally held only by the Unwá,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: is that the existence of time travel technology

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: represents a threat to the history of every race in the Symbiotry.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: For this reason, these races feel that all existing time machines should be completely dismantled.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Following the arrest of Agent 5,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: the Lôxôni changed their allegiance from petitioning for the release of time travel technology

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: to requesting its destruction.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: They were joined by the Krynn, for whom this represents a break in their long-standing tradition of fervently supporting every race's right to sovereignty over its own technologies.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: The Lôxôni now proclaim that if not destroyed,

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: the technology must at the very least be put in the safe keeping of an elder race of the Symbiotry.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: They cite security as their main concern.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Like the others that share their goal, they feel that humanity lacks the necessary discretion

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: to control such a powerful tool.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: As a side note, it should be mentioned that the Lôxôni themselves are among the eldest races of the Symbiotry.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Despite being recently abandoned by the Krynn,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: two of humanity's staunchest supporters, the Cyrollans and the Ssar,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: have continued to defend our right to autonomy over time travel technology.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Like those that favored dismantling it,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: these two races would rather leave their pasts buried than risk losing it all together.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: But unlike the others, the Cyrollans and Ssar believe that humanity harbors a maturity beyond its years

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: and can be entrusted with preserving the sanctity of history.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: In fact, they suggest that our closeness to our violent past makes us even better suited to manage time travel,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: as the dire consequences of the misuse of technology still stain our racial memory.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Unfortunately, theirs is a minority opinion.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The prevailing response to this argument is that Earth's record with time travel speaks for itself.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: In just ten years, there have already been incidents of deliberate historical sabotage,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: the latest of which allegedly involving an agent of the Temporal Security Agency.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Our benefactors, however,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: dismissed the Elliott Sinclair and Gage Blackwood incidents as aberrant acts by disturbed individuals,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: rather than a weakness of humanity as a whole.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: And they ask, as a sign of good faith and trust in the newest member of the Symbiotry,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: that the future of time travel technology be left to our discretion.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Despite the arguments made by the Symbiotry envoys,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: the general opinion of the heads of ministry, so far, appears unswayed.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Michael Rozhenko of the Northwest Asia Collective rebutted that

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: the danger of time travel falling into the wrong hands and being used to change history, however slight,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: is still too great to even consider releasing the technology.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: It must be realized that time travel has not only the power to unlock the secrets of history,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: but also unparalleled potential for destruction.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Few could argue that it would be foolish to give such a tool to anyone, regardless of its intended use.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: On the other hand, it's also too late for it to be destroyed,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: as was pointed out by Chancellor of Law Rick Allen,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: when he stated that the technology has already been created and can therefore be recreated.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Chancellor Allen emphasized his point by attesting that if all known time travel technology were destroyed,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: and a new time machine built without government knowledge or approval,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: there would be no way to intervene in the actions of the illicit time traveler.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: He would have free rein to rewrite history to his liking.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Unfortunately, such scenarios are all too likely,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: as was proven by the Elliott Sinclair incident and the current trial of Gage Blackwood.

subtitles.speaker: Announcer
subtitles.text: INN will return after a word from our sponsor.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: The ongoing saga of Gage Blackwood took a frightening twist this morning

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: when the agent of the Deep Time Unit broke house arrest to jump nine years back in time.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Fortunately, the illicit time jump was detected and he was immediately apprehended

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: by Agent Eight of the Temporal Protectorate.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Although it's still not clear how and why Blackwood obtained the TSA jumpsuit,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Temporal Security Agency officials did say that no distortion ripples have yet been detected,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: and that there is no reason whatsoever to believe that Blackwood has altered history in any way.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Our Lisa Long has a report from TSA administrative headquarters.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: In a strange turn of events that can only be described as unimaginable,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: the highly decorated Gage Blackwood, better known as Agent 5 of the Deep Time Unit,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: has been arrested and put on trial for the crime of historical sabotage.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: We apologize for the lack of trial footage,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: but because of the sensitive nature of the material being presented,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: no recording equipment has been allowed into the tribunal wing of the United Ministry Complex,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: where the trial is being held.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The drama unfolded three weeks ago when Agent 2 of the Temporal Protectorate

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: discovered four distortion ripples while conducting an unscheduled historical scan.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: As it turned out, the dates of the ripples exactly coincided with

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: times to which Agent 5 had been sent for research purposes.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The agent immediately contacted his supervisors, and, on their orders,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: three agents were sent to apprehend Agent 5, who offered no resistance.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Later that day, more evidence was found in Blackwood's locker,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: suggesting that he had disobeyed Temple Security Agency directives for personal gain.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Unless deemed absolutely necessary,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: the TSA will not send agents to investigate or restore the distortions

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: as any further tampering with history may cause adverse effects,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: possibly even turning the ripples into full reality distortion waves.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: I have with me now Commissioner Jack Baldwin of the Temporal Security Agency,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: who's coming to us live from TSA administrative headquarters.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Commissioner, thank you for joining us.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Now, the first and most obvious question is:

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Are you confident in your arrest of Gage Blackwood as the perpetrator of this crime?

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: We had to arrest Agent 5 because of the evidence, not because we think he did it.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: There was an obvious transgression. Someone was responsible for it.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: So, we arrested the person to whom the evidence pointed.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: Now it's up to the courts to determine whether or not he's guilty.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: So you believe he's innocent?

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: Absolutely.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: I've known Gage ever since he joined the TSA. In fact, I'm the one who recruited him.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: Gage Blackwood is a member of an endangered species. Gage Blackwood is a hero.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: He has put his life on the line many times to prevent this exact thing from happening.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: There's absolutely no way he would have abused his position at the risk of a single life,

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: let alone history as we know it.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: Now, it just doesn't make sense.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Mr. Blackwood has been an agent for quite a while now, thirteen years, I believe.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Is it possible that the temptation just became too great for him to bear?

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: No. Gage has as committed to his duty now as he was back when he apprehended Elliot Sinclair.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: He was and he is our finest agent.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Okay, let's assume for a minute that he did do it.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Knowing that he would be facing life imprisonment on Vega Thalon, do you feel that he would plead guilty?

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: First of all, it's ... it's a moot point because he *didn't* do it.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: But, presuming he did, knowing Gage, I'd say he had a damn good reason.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: And he would have confessed immediately.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: He wouldn't have pretended innocence not for one minute.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: Bottom line, Gage Blackwood is no criminal.

subtitles.speaker: Commissioner Baldwin
subtitles.text: Gage Blackwood is a hero.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Okay, commissioner, it looks like we're out of time. Thank you.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: With us now is William Daughton, the TSA Chief Technician.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: He joins us live from the Temporal Security Agency administrative headquarters.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Thank you for joining us, Mr. Daughton.

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: Thank you, Mark.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: You've known Gage Blackwood for many years, and I understand that the two of you are good friends.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Do you think he's guilty?

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: Absolutely not.

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: The thought that he could be guilty never even crossed my mind.

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: I mean, friend or no, here you've got someone who's dedicated his whole life to protecting history

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: and now stands accused of violating it.

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: That's ridiculous!

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: And if you don't believe me, look at his record. The man's a decorated hero.

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: You can't overlook that fact just because it doesn't fit neatly

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: into the story the prosecution's is trying to sell.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Isn't it true you testified that no one else made a time jump to any of the altered historical locations?

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: No, actually I testified the scanners didn't register anyone making a time jump to those locations.

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: The computers are only as intelligent as their human programmers.

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: Now, I believe it's possible that someone could have shadowed Agent 5's jumps.

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: If a second time traveler were to make a jump

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: within a few seconds of the first and to the same location,

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: the chronolog scanners probably wouldn't recognize it  as a second jump.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Have you been able to test this theory?

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: No. Not yet. It's ... it's too dangerous.

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: If two people were to travel through the same null time tunnel and land in the exact same place,

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: well, their matter would mix and that would kill them.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Then you believe that someone found a way around this?

subtitles.speaker: Chief Technician Daughton
subtitles.text: It's possible, yes.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Okay, well, thank you for your insights, Mr. Daughton.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: If Blackwood is indeed guilty, he has altered more than just the past.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: The future, too, will likely feel the results of his actions.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: The Deep Time Unit will probably be discontinued before ever realizing its full potential.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: But there is an even greater issue at stake.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: That is whether the Temporal Security Agency itself is more of a risk than a safety measure.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Many feel that it should be shut down and everything related to time travel destroyed.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Others argue that the technology has already been invented,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: so there's nothing stopping it from being reinvented for the wrong reasons.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: So, in their opinion, the Temporal Security Agency must remain operational

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: to safeguard against future acts of historical sabotage.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: In a last ditch effort to stay afloat, the Louvre Art Museum held an auction of unprecedented scale yesterday.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: The museum was forced to sell off many of its older collections to pay off creditors

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: and to raise funds desperately needed for renovations to the facility.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: In a fervent display of support, the art community rallied around the historic landmark,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: showing that the museum itself is every bit as valuable an artifact as any of the works of art it contains.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: The auction was an astounding success, raising 138.5 billion credits,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: easily surpassing the 100 billion credit goal.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: This windfall was due in large part to one generous bidder who preferred to remain unidentified.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Martin Walker is standing by with a live report from the Louvre.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Thanks, Mark. I'm standing inside the historic Louvre Museum in Paris.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Behind me sits one of the few pieces to survive yesterday's extensive art auction.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Items up for auction included artifacts and works of art from many of the Louvre's oldest collections,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: including the da Vinci exhibit, the ancient Egyptian, and Toltec Mayan exhibits.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Four particular items were snapped up by a generous bidder, who paid much more than the asking price.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The bidder's identity is unknown,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: but it is assumed to be an art enthusiast who didn't want to see the Louvre shut down.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: There are rumors, however,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: that the buyer may actually have been acting on behalf of another race in the Symbiotry,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: which, according to the Earth History Preservation Act of 2322, would be illegal.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: We're told an investigation may follow.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Museum sources that I spoke to speculated that the revenue from the auction

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: will be enough to keep the Louvre in operation for at least the next five years.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: However, they warned me that the price of admission may go up in order to help cover operating costs.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: A small price to pay for such a wealth of human history and culture.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: The heads of Ministry will continue to meet with Symbiotry representatives today

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: in the assembly hall of the United Ministry Complex.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: These talks were requested by several member races

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: as a forum in which to discuss the place of time travel technology in the Symbiotry of Peaceful Beings.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Today marks the beginning of the third week of negotiations, yet there is still no end in sight.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Sarah Michaels is standing by at the United Ministry Complex with a report.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Thank you, Mark.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The main factor protracting the discussions

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: is the inability of the Symbiotry to decide what should be done with the technology.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The representatives have formed three distinct factions

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: whose strongly opposing views have caused them to remain tenaciously entrenched in a deadlock.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: While one group believes we are committing the unforgivable act of hoarding a vital technology,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: a second supports the Symbiotry tenet that each race has sovereignty over its own technologies.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: The third contingent, which has grown in strength since the arrest of Agent 5,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: contends that time travel represents a threat to every race of the Symbiotry and should be destroyed altogether.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Even though most attending races strongly disagree with humanity's sole ownership of the technology,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: our heads of ministry refuse to acknowledge their arguments,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: citing its inevitable misuse as their foremost concern.

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: Therefore, barring Symbiotry action,

subtitles.speaker: Reporter
subtitles.text: it is unlikely that the status of time travel as a proprietary technology of Earth will change.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: In a late-breaking update from the technology discussions,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: the Krynn ambassador, Icarus, moments ago stormed out of the talks,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: apparently frustrated with the lack of progress.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: The conflict began when the ambassador said, quote,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: "Even the Krynn can no longer deny the truth of the situation", and that they don't understand

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: how anyone could defend our right to keep such a hazardous technology.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Until last week, Icarus maintained the Krynn's usual position,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: that each race should be allowed complete autonomy over its own technologies.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: But their attitude changed soon after Agent 5 was arrested.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: Since then, the Krynn ambassador has repeatedly tried to gain the support of all the other envoys

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: in fighting for the abolishment of time travel.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: When this last plea once again met with resistance, Icarus launched into a tirade,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: exclaiming that, if they had known better,

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: they would not have voted to let such an obstinate and naive race as humanity into the Symbiotry.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: He then abruptly departed.

subtitles.speaker: News Anchor
subtitles.text: The talks will go on despite the Krynn withdrawal.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: The events surrounding the arrest of Agent 5 bring back, for most, memories of the Elliott Sinclair incident.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: That historic day 10 years ago could have turned out much differently if it weren't for Agent 5 of the Temporal Protectorate.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: After building the first-ever functional time machine,

subtitles.speaker: Arthur

subtitles.text: Frustrated, exasperated, and on the verge of insanity,

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: he sent each of his three robot minions back in time to change the course of history.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: The first, he sent to create a nuclear scare that would prevent world unification and prolong the Cold War.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: The second was to destroy the Morimoto Mars colony and make it look like the work of an alien race.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: And the third, Sinclair sent to kill Dr. Enrique Castillo,

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: the individual who was most influential in convincing humanity of the benefits of joining the Symbiotry.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: His backup plan, should his robots have failed, was to assassinate the Cyrollan delegate.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: It was our good fortune that Agent 5 was on duty at the Temporal Security Annex that day.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: He detected the temporal distortions, stopped each of the androids, and then apprehended Sinclair himself.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: That fateful morning made a hero of Agent 5 and spawned the blockbuster holoflick, The Journeyman Project.

subtitles.text: Elliott Sinclair was put on trial and found guilty of all charges.

subtitles.speaker: Arthur
subtitles.text: He was sentenced to life imprisonment on Vega Thalon and hasn't been heard from since.
